A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MATHCHECK work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including the rendered heatmaps, and corresponding methods, experiments, and examples can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on MATHCHECK-GSM and MATHCHECK-GEO, correlation and behavioral analyses, and human-checked data-generation pass rates.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations of further language and multimodal models in Tables 1–2 and the appendix heatmaps.

M1.justification: The mathematical checklist, construction pipeline, and generation prompts remain unchanged. Section 5 and Appendix E.2 introduce a limited code-generation adaptation: scenario-understanding variants request the same function in another programming language, illustrated by Python-to-Java conversion. This is an illustrated procedural adaptation, not an experimentally validated replacement method.

E1.justification: The evaluated mathematical datasets, tasks, languages, and robustness variants are retained, as are the GSM1k and mathematical-text compression analyses. Date understanding and code generation in Section 5 and Appendix E are illustrative checklist constructions; no model evaluations on these additional domains are reported.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 expand from 20 to 26 LLMs and from 11 to 17 MLLMs. GSM additions include o1-preview, o1-mini, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, and Llama-3.1-8B/70B. GEO adds GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Qwen2-VL-7B/72B, MiniCPM-Llama3-V-2.5, and LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: Table 3 corrects GSM answerable-judging and outcome-judging counts from 358 to 258 per problem variant, making them consistent with the retained 129 groups and 3,096 total samples. This revises reported sample counts without establishing resampling or rerunning. Metrics, shot settings, and decoding limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 examines possible GPT-rewriter bias by comparing overall performance with original-problem/outcome-judging performance in Table 7. Its scores already appeared in v1, but the bias-focused comparison is new. Existing correlation, complexity, prompting, and mathematical-model analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Pearson-correlation and RMSE reporting in Figures 3–4 remains unchanged; the added comparisons use point estimates.

E6.justification: All retained model scores in Tables 1–2 are unchanged, but twelve model/benchmark entries are added. On GSM, o1-preview and o1-mini score 93.2 and 92.7, above GPT-4o's retained 92.0. Figure 5 also changes the Llama-2-70B-base matrix to duplicate MetaMath's matrix, unlike v1; its original-problem-solving value changes from 37.2 to 77.5. Another inconsistency appears in v2: Section 3.3 reports Qwen-VL-70B at 60.4, while Table 2 lists Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct at 61.4.

T1.justification: Neither version presents a formal theoretical development. The retained conceptual task definitions and mathematical examples are not supplemented by new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims about comprehensive mathematical evaluation and closer alignment with reasoning ability remain. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion newly highlight applicability beyond mathematics to commonsense reasoning and code generation, broadening the claimed scope without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly acknowledges possible generator self-bias and argues that manual checking and comparative rankings make it acceptable. Section 3.3 narrows the criticism of open-source visual reasoning to smaller models. Section 4 replaces the explanation involving abbreviated few-shot reasoning and weak Plan-and-Solve performance with few-shot sensitivity and a recommendation for zero-shot CoT or Plan-and-Solve.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the seed difficulty range as 2–8 reasoning steps and describes the original-problem/outcome-judging subset as rule-generated without GPT rewriting. Appendix D identifies the additional model versions. Existing evaluation and generation prompt templates and decoding hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: References are added for the new models, BIG-bench, OlympicArena, and Arena-Hard/MT-Bench in the generator-bias discussion. The underlying positioning against single-task mathematical benchmarks and the motivation from CheckList remain. Conversion to author–year citations is a presentation change.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5, an appendix contents page, and the bias subsection, while relocating the existing prompt and case appendices from E/F to F/G. Introduction, results commentary, related work, and conclusion receive localized rewrites. Most methodological prose and all original prompt and case content are preserved.

P2.justification: The document is broadly reformatted, including title and headings, table-caption placement, and numbered prompt/case listings. Heatmaps are redrawn with explicit task and variant labels, and the GSM heatmaps are split across two figures. Tables 1–2 are expanded and redistributed; Table 7 and the two new checklist diagrams are added.

improvement.justification: The expanded model comparisons, corrected sample counts, explicit heatmap labels, and generator-bias discussion improve usefulness and clarity. However, v2 introduces a material reporting defect: Figure 5 duplicates MetaMath's results under the Llama-2 baseline, undermining the retained behavioral comparison. The new Qwen prose/table mismatch adds another reliability problem. These benefits and harms leave the net overall quality direction uncertain.
